governanceNotes: D1 batch 59 (2026-09-26): one bounded association edge authored - malunion-nonunion-of-fractures to post-traumatic-osteoarthritis (rank 1) - classified ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, and hypothesizedOnly:true. The proposition rests on the geriatric tibial-malunion secondary-knee-osteoarthritis case (PMID 42211638), the proximal-tibia malunion management review (PMID 41438797), and the tibial plateau malunion corrective-osteotomy case (PMID 41837061).

Counter-evidence and caveat screens recorded 2026-09-26: (i) evidence class - one case plus two management narratives without incidence denominators by deformity magnitude, site, or angle; (ii) confound record - intra-articular fracture damage predisposes to osteoarthritis independently of alignment, and primary age-related osteoarthritis overlaps the older presentations; (iii) semantic boundary - the unexplained-chronic-pain identity's unexplained-etiology requirement excludes mechanically explained malunion pain, so no pain edge was authored; (iv) sibling-window discipline - tarsal-metatarsal-malunion-nonunion and mandibular-nonunion (both dispositioned safe drafts) and the published knee-injury, acl-injury, and mallet-finger PTOA windows keep their own evidence and none is recycled (ME-29).

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Malunion of fractures documents secondary osteoarthritis at case plus specialty-review level: the geriatric case of severe knee osteoarthritis secondary to a longstanding tibial malunion healed at 57.2-degree procurvatum and 30.9-degree valgus after failed fixation states that persistent tibial malunion introduces varus or valgus forces predisposing to knee compartment overload and promoting osteoarthritis (PMID 42211638), the proximal-tibia malunion management review directs that the mechanical axis be restored as soon as safe to prevent or slow progression of post-traumatic osteoarthritis (PMID 41438797), and the tibial plateau malunion case presenting two years after trauma with valgus deformity and articular depression underwent corrective osteotomy explicitly to prevent progression of osteoarthritis (PMID 41837061); the relationship is recorded as documented biomechanical sequel only.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual: the located material is one case and two management-level reviews where joint-surface incongruity, deformity magnitude and plane, limb alignment, activity level, and fixation history all require individual radiographic review before any osteoarthritis attribution to the malunion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Fracture healed in malalignment shifts the mechanical axis and concentrates joint contact load on a smaller articular area so cartilage overload, progressive degeneration, and post-traumatic osteoarthritis result, the overload route stated in the malunion case and the proximal-tibia review whose axis-restoration rationale presupposes it, but whether this route produced any individual osteoarthritis remains hypothesized until dated weight-bearing radiographs and alignment measurements are reviewed.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The association is supported at single-case plus narrative-review class only: the strongest anchor is one Cureus case with limited follow-up and no objective postoperative alignment data, the two reviews are management narratives rather than incidence cohorts, and no located study quantifies osteoarthritis incidence by malunion site, angle, or alignment deviation.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: No incidence cohort quantifies post-traumatic osteoarthritis risk by malunion site, deformity magnitude, or axis deviation; primary and age-related osteoarthritis overlap the presentation in older patients; intra-articular fracture damage predisposes to osteoarthritis independently of alignment; and surgical correction, activity change, and joint replacement all alter the observed course.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: intra-articular fracture step-off arthrosis independent of alignment
post-traumatic osteoarthritis from the original injury without malunion (the published knee-injury and mallet-finger PTOA windows, not recycled per ME-29)

suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY on the biomechanical-malalignment precedent mirroring the published post-traumatic-osteoarthritis windows with malunion-specific evidence only: the geriatric tibial-malunion case documents severe knee osteoarthritis arising in a 57.2-degree procurvatum and 30.9-degree valgus malalignment with the paper stating persistent malunion introduces varus or valgus forces promoting osteoarthritis (PMID 42211638), the proximal-tibia malunion review frames mechanical-axis restoration as the means to prevent or slow PTOA progression (PMID 41438797), and the tibial plateau malunion case documents valgus deformity with articular depression requiring corrective osteotomy to prevent osteoarthritis progression (PMID 41837061); because the evidence is one case plus management narratives without incidence denominators by deformity magnitude, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only and routes individual claims through dated weight-bearing alignment imaging with primary-osteoarthritis and original-injury arthrosis exclusion.
